documented_reaction: The dollar fell 17.4% against the yen in the quarter; on 7 October USD/JPY fell 6.7% as speculative accounts deleveraged and covered losses incurred in other markets.
mechanism: Cross-market loss coverage and balance-sheet deleveraging

documented_reaction: Rising FX volatility unwound carry positions; the yen appreciated, higher-yield currencies depreciated, stock prices plunged, credit spreads widened and JGB market liquidity deteriorated.
mechanism: Funding constraints, forced deleveraging and safe-asset demand

documented_reaction: The Nikkei fell 10.6% on 15 March. The yen reached the 76-77 range before coordinated intervention; BOJ later reported USD/JPY around 85-86 and temporarily reduced option-implied concern over further yen appreciation.
mechanism: Disaster shock, repatriation expectations, retail stop-losses and coordinated policy reversal

documented_reaction: FX swap basis spreads widened to levels last seen in the GFC; central-bank swap use reached $446bn by 30 April, led by the BOJ at $220bn and ECB at $143bn.
mechanism: Global dollar shortage and bank/dealer balance-sheet demand

documented_reaction: MOF bought yen on four dates for a total of ¥15.323tn. The intervention phase preceded the July reversal in yen depreciation and changed incentives for leveraged speculators.

JPY appreciated, MXN and other investment currencies weakened, TOPIX posted double-digit losses, TOPIX banks had their worst one-day loss in 40 years, VIX briefly exceeded 60 pre-market, yields fell and crypto faced margin pressure. Credit widening was comparatively modest and re-compressed.
mechanism: US labor shock plus BOJ repricing, crowded positions, options hedging and margin calls

documented_reaction: MOF reported ¥11.7349tn of yen buying on 30 April, 4 May and 6 May, followed by a ¥15.3993tn aggregate for 30 July-26 August. Public daily detail for the latter window was not yet available at the research cutoff.
mechanism: Large official spot-market demand; later-window attribution remains unresolved
